lead.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
lead.note: SpaceX has caught its Starship spacecraft, and NPR reports that the company made history in doing so. The vehicle returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion. It carefully lowered itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it. In plain terms, the launch tower itself held the spacecraft as it came back down. The catch is the central fact in the report, and the summary states it plainly. For a reader who follows space and engineering, this is a notable moment, because it shows a large machine and a fixed structure working together at the end of a flight. The short report gives no further detail on the mission, so the wider meaning will depend on later coverage. It is today's most significant science and technology story.

week.summary:
Anthropic had a busy week. It released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 (w27, w26). Mythos is limited to organizations verified through Anthropic's programs. Fable gets a fast mode with up to 2.5x output speed at higher per-token prices (w31). Anthropic also filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO and launched a roadshow (w76, w56). It put a portion of its shares into a new Public Benefit Fund (w57) and expanded its GSA partnership (w6). Claude Platform added self-hosted Managed Agents (w102). In design software, AI features came to V-Ray, Enscape, Trimble and Rhino 9, and SketchUp 2027 improved its Revit interoperability (w20, w21, w45, w95, w70).

In world news, US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended with a prisoner exchange agreement, and US envoys then met Putin (w79, w109). The White House says Trump, Putin and Xi plan a joint meeting in China next week (w123). Trump said more US attacks on Iran are highly unlikely (w37). After the midterms, Congress returned before Democrats take control in January (w5), and House Republicans chose Jim Jordan as leader (w61). On Friday a nationwide ground stop led to more than 400 cancelled flights at Hartsfield-Jackson the next morning (w157, w147). A building collapse in Brooklyn killed at least two people (w89).

In sports, the Rockets are 10-3 after Alperen Sengun scored 43 points (w124). The 49ers beat the Raiders 38-17 and traded for Keenan Allen (w2, w80). The Braves agreed to a deal with Evan Phillips (w103), and both champions kept their titles at UFC 334 (w146). SpaceX caught its Starship (w145).
